summary: BA spec for §5.16 (inline LaTeX $...$ not rendered) is technically sound. All four claimed files exist, all code-level claims (regex absence, type discriminant absence, LatexRenderer displayMode hard-coded to true, no inline prop) are verified against the actual worktree source. Scope correctly distinguishes inline $...$ (broken) from block $$...$$ (working). One minor concern flagged below but not blocking.

checks.note: Regex confirmed: 4 alternations for bold/italic/link/code. No dollar-sign case exists anywhere in the file (lines 1-88).

checks.ba_claim: MarkdownSpan type has no 'latex' variant in styles union (parseMarkdown.ts:42)
checks.note: Confirmed: styles is a string-literal union with 4 values, none of which is 'latex'. The MarkdownSpan type has only { styles, text, url } fields — no discriminant field for content type.

objections.finding: BA's Technical Hints offer TWO approaches for span model change: (a) add 'latex' to styles enum, (b) add a discriminant field like 'latexContent?: string'. BA says dev should pick, but dev may pick (a) which is semantically wrong (latex is content-type, not a style). BA should have made a stronger prescription.
objections.evidence: ba-spec-20260424-143000-1.md lines 129-134: 'add latex-inline span discriminant ... or add a new type: latex field' + Span model choice guidance
objections.recommendation: Not blocking — BA does note 'which is semantically a style, not a content type' and pushes toward the discriminant-field approach. Dev should follow that direction.

objections.finding: BA's Edge Cases mention a heuristic regex '$[^ $]([^$]*?)[^ $]$' but this regex has issues: single-char content case claim is contradicted by '[^ $]([^$]*?)[^ $]' which requires TWO non-space characters. BA should clarify or let dev design the regex.
objections.evidence: ba-spec-20260424-143000-1.md line 95: 'A safe heuristic: $[^ $]([^$]*?)[^ $]$ (content must not start or end with whitespace; must have at least one character; single-char content is allowed if not a digit directly following $)'
objections.recommendation: Not blocking — BA notes 'Dev should use a conservative regex and document the limitation.' Dev has latitude to design the actual regex.

objections.finding: BA acknowledges uncertainty about inline KaTeX on React Native: 'On native, inline LaTeX will likely need a small <WebView> or dangerouslySetInnerHTML <span> (web only). Dev should verify...' This is good honest flagging but leaves a potential gap for R6 (native rendering).
objections.recommendation: BA correctly flags; dev must verify. For a web-first dev-overnight verification cycle this is acceptable since Playwright tests run on web platform.
